task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hello... yes, hi. I'm having a bit of trouble with my phone. I can't send picture messages — you know, the ones with photos of my grandchildren. It's been a few hours now and I just can't figure out what's wrong. Can you help me?

turns.thought:
Of course — I'd be happy to help you get picture messages working again. To start, I'll need to look up your account.

Could you please confirm your phone number (or your full name and date of birth)?
turns.execution_output:
User: It's John Smith. My phone number is 555-123-2002. 

Oh, and I should mention — I'm in France right now, visiting. I don't know if that matters, but... well, I thought I should say something.

turns.thought: Thanks, John — let me look up your account now.
I've found your account. Let me run some diagnostics on your phone.

turns.thought:
I found your account, Mr. Smith, and I've checked your line and billing. Good news: your line is Active, your bill is issued but not yet overdue, and you're well within your data allowance (8.7 GB of 15 GB).

To keep troubleshooting, I need to check the settings on your phone itself. Please open the **diagnostic panel on your device** (the tool list on your phone) and run these for me, one at a time:

1. **check_status_bar**
2. **check_network_status**
3. **check_sim_status**

Tell me what each one shows and we'll go from there. In the meantime, since you're in France, I can already note one important thing: line 555-123-2002 already has international roaming enabled on the account, so roaming shouldn't be the blocker.

Also — could you tell me whether regular calls and plain text messages are working?
turns.execution_output: User: Oh, alright. Let me try to find this... diagnostic panel, you said? I'll do the first one.

turns.thought:
Great — thanks for checking those. The SIM being active is a good sign, and "Data Roaming: No" is very likely our culprit.

Here's the situation:

- **On your account**, international roaming is **already enabled** on line 555-123-2002, and per our roaming policy it's provided at no cost for customers traveling outside their home network — so switching it on won't add a charge to your bill.
- **On your phone**, though, the Data Roaming switch itself is currently **OFF**. Even with roaming enabled on the account, the phone won't use data over the French network until that switch is on. And picture messages (MMS) need a data connection to send.

**Please do this for me:**

Use **toggle_roaming** on your device to turn **Data Roaming ON**, then try sending one of the grandkid pictures again.

**And yes, please do try a regular text message** — that's a helpful clue. If plain texts also fail, the problem is broader than picture messaging and we'll look at it differently than if only the photos fail.

One other thing while you're at it — please run **check_status_bar** again after turning roaming on and tell me what signal and network type it shows (something like 4G or 5G). That'll tell me whether you're properly connected to the local network.

Take your time, and let me know how it goes.
turns.execution_output: User: All right, I'll turn that roaming thing on. You're sure it won't cost me extra? Okay... doing it now.

turns.thought:
I'm sorry this is frustrating — let's keep at it. First, two quick reassurances:

- **Your photos are not lost.** Picture messages that fail to send stay in your messaging app / photo gallery on your phone. Nothing gets deleted, and they'll be there waiting once we get this working.
- **Turning on Data Roaming won't cost you extra.** International roaming is enabled on your line at no cost, and it was already active on the account side before you flipped the switch on the phone.

You've now confirmed the app itself reports it **cannot send MMS**, which is a useful, concrete clue. Let's work through the remaining known causes.

**Please run these on your device and tell me exactly what they say:**

1. **check_apn_settings** — this shows your APN name and the MMSC URL. The MMSC is the server that handles picture messages; if it's missing or wrong, MMS simply won't send. This is the single most common cause.
2. **check_status_bar** — I need to see the **network type** (e.g. 4G, 5G, 3G, 2G) and whether it shows **Data Enabled**. 2G in particular can't carry picture messages.
3. **check_wifi_calling_status** — Wi-Fi Calling being ON can sometimes interfere with MMS.

Tell me what those three show and I'll tell you the next fix. We're narrowing it down, I promise.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, thank you for saying that about the photos. That's a relief. Let me do these three things.

turns.thought:
Yes — you found it. That "Not Set" is exactly what's broken, and it's the answer to your photos question too.

**What that means in plain terms:** picture messages don't travel the same way as regular texts. They need to be sent through a special server — that's the "MMSC." Your phone needs the address of that server to send a photo, and right now the address field is blank. So your phone has no idea where to send the pictures. Everything else checks out great: excellent 5G signal, data on, roaming on, Wi-Fi Calling off (that's fine, leave it).

**Please do these two steps, in this order:**

1. Use **reset_apn_settings** on your device — this restores the correct settings, including the missing MMSC address.
2. Use **reboot_device** — **this part is required.** The new settings don't take effect until the phone restarts. (Wait for it to fully come back on, a minute or so.)

After it restarts, **make sure Data Roaming is still ON** (the reboot can sometimes reset it), then try sending a picture of your grandchildren again.

Go ahead and let me know how it goes.
turns.execution_output: User: All right... "reset" — that doesn't delete anything, does it? Okay, I'll trust you. Doing the first one.

turns.thought:
Wonderful — I'm so glad the photo got through! You're very welcome, and no apology needed at all.

**Yes, that blank address was the whole problem.** Your phone was trying to send pictures without knowing which server to send them through. Resetting the APN settings put the correct MMSC address back, and the reboot made it take effect.

**You're all set.** I just re-verified your line and everything looks good:

- Line 555-123-2002: **Active**
- **International roaming: enabled** (at no cost, for your time in France)
- Data usage: **8.7 GB of 15 GB** this cycle — plenty of room
- Your current bill is issued but **not due until February 19**, so nothing overdue

**To keep it working while you're in France:**
- Leave **Data Roaming ON** until you're back home — it's needed for data and picture messages abroad, and there's no extra charge.
- If a phone update ever asks to reset network settings, or if picture messages stop again, the same two steps will fix it: **reset_apn_settings**, then **reboot_device**.
- Your photos were never at risk — they live in your phone's gallery, and any sent messages remain in your messaging app.

Enjoy your visit, and enjoy sending those pictures to your daughter. If anything else comes up, just let me know and I'll help you sort it out.
turns.execution_output:
User: Thank you, that's all very clear. I'll leave the roaming on while I'm here, and I wrote down those two steps in case it happens again — well, I'll try to remember anyway.

I really appreciate your help. My daughter will be happy to get the pictures. Have a good day!
